newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's NBK 1996 profit seen up 7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's NBK 1996 profit seen up 7 pct.

text.p: National Bank of Kuwait (NBK), the country's largest commercial bank, is expected to report a seven percent rise in 1996 net profit to about 70 million dinars ($234 million), al-Rai al-Aam newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The daily, quoting a "closely related source", said the the bank, the oldest commercial bank in the Arabian Peninsula, was expected to pay a cash dividend of up to 50 percent for 1996 compared to 40 percent the previous year.

NBK shares are currently trading at 650 fils, unchanged from Monday's close on the Kuwait Stock Exchange. The banking sector has been active in recent weeks as some investors are expecting strong end-of-year results and high dividends by Kuwaiti banks.
In July NBK recorded a 17 percent in rise net profit to 35.2 million dinars in the first half of 1996 compared to the same period in 1995. Net profit rose 19 percent last year to 65.5 million dinars.
NBK shares closed Tuesday at 650 fils with a day high of 660.
